usageNotes: Use this to register a new LDAP authentication realm in Proxmox Datacenter Manager, enabling centralized directory-based login for PDM users. The calling token or user must hold the Realm.Allocate privilege on the access/domains path. After creation, run a user sync (post_access_domains_realm_sync) to populate users from the directory before they can log in.

examples.summary: Create an Active Directory-backed LDAP realm with STARTTLS and attribute mapping

tips: The realm name must be 2–32 characters and match /^(?:[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9.\-_]*)$/ — choose a short, stable identifier since renaming requires delete+recreate.
For Active Directory, set user-attr to 'sAMAccountName'; for standard OpenLDAP, use 'uid'.
Use mode 'ldaps' (port 636) or 'ldap+starttls' (port 389) in production — plain 'ldap' transmits bind credentials in cleartext.
Set verify=true with a capath pointing to your internal CA cert when using STARTTLS or LDAPS against an internal PKI.
The filter param accepts standard LDAP filter syntax; use it to exclude disabled accounts or restrict to a specific OU.
After creation, the realm won't have any PDM users yet — trigger a sync immediately via post_access_domains_realm_sync.
